points.description: First advantage, stated precisely: separating declaration from definition makes the code clearer and easier for the reader to understand (readability/clarity), OR separates abstraction (interface/declaration) from implementation (definition).
points.partial_credit: Half only if the idea is clearly more than half stated (e.g. says 'clearer' without saying for the reader/understanding); otherwise 0.

points.description: Second distinct advantage, stated precisely: allows easy changing, debugging and overriding of functions, OR enhances modularity of the code (whichever differs from the advantage credited in P1).
points.partial_credit: Half only if more than half is stated precisely (e.g. 'easy changing' of functions with no further link, or 'modular' stated vaguely); otherwise 0.

rubric.notes: Two distinct advantages are needed, each from the model answer: clarity/readability, easy changing/debugging/overriding, modularity, or separating abstraction from implementation. Each must be stated precisely with the right term; vague statements such as 'better code' or 'saves time' earn nothing. A wrong statement within an advantage, or two wordings of the same advantage, earns only one point at most; a wrong extra advantage costs the point it is paired with.
